advertisement-disclaimers@2022-06-09: A disclaimer can clarify an advertising claim, but cannot contradict a material claim, correct a misleading claim, hide material information or conceal commercial intent. It should be prominent and legible and use the claim's language and font.
complainant-definition@2020-07-20: A consumer, a registered consumer association, government, the Central Authority or consumers with the same interest can qualify as a complainant. If the consumer dies, a legal heir or representative can qualify; for a minor, a parent or legal guardian can qualify.
complaint-procedure@2020-07-20: After admitting a complaint about goods, the District Commission sends it to the other party within 21 days of admission. That party normally has 30 days to respond, with up to 15 extra days if the Commission grants an extension. The Commission can arrange testing if the alleged defect needs laboratory analysis.
consumer-definition@2020-07-20: Buying goods or paying for services, including online, generally makes you a consumer. Resale and commercial-purpose purchases are excluded, but that exclusion does not cover goods you buy and use exclusively to earn your livelihood through self-employment.
dark-pattern-confirm-shaming@2023-11-30: Confirm shaming uses fear, shame, ridicule or guilt to push a purchase or keep a subscription. For example, an opt-out button may insult or guilt-trip someone for declining an optional purchase.
dark-pattern-false-urgency@2023-11-30: False urgency uses fake stock shortages, misleading popularity claims or invented deadlines to pressure people to buy or act immediately. A genuine low-stock warning or deadline is not false urgency on its own.
ecommerce-platform-response-time@2020-07: The platform's grievance officer must acknowledge a complaint within 48 hours and resolve it within one month of receiving it.
enforcement-of-orders@2020-07-20: A Consumer Commission enforces its own order like a civil court decree. Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure applies as far as possible, with references to a decree treated as references to the Commission's order.
inventory-platform-information@2020-07-2: An online retailer selling its own inventory must show the total price as one figure and break out all compulsory and optional charges, including applicable taxes and delivery charges. It must also display returns, warranty, shipping and payment terms and give each complaint a tracking number.
mediation-settlement@2020-07-20: If mediation settles some or all issues, the parties or their authorised representatives sign the written terms. The mediator sends the signed agreement and a settlement report to the Commission. If no agreement is reached, the mediator reports that too.
nch-prelitigation-limits@2026-11-01: Contacting the National Consumer Helpline is not the same as filing a case before a Consumer Commission. The helpline tries to resolve the complaint before litigation. If it does not resolve the issue to your satisfaction, you can approach the appropriate Commission.
product-liability-exceptions@2020-07-20: A product-liability action cannot be brought against a product seller if the product was misused, altered or modified at the time of harm. Section 87 also lists separate exceptions to a manufacturer's liability for failing to warn or instruct users.
product-seller-liability@2020-07-20: A seller that did not manufacture the product can be liable if it made its own express warranty independent of the manufacturer's, and the product's failure to meet that warranty caused harm. Section 86 lists other grounds too; selling the product alone does not establish liability.
recording-mediation-settlement@2020-07-2: If mediation settles only part of a consumer dispute, the Commission records the agreement on the settled issues and continues hearing the unresolved issues. If nothing settles, it continues hearing all issues.
reference-to-mediation@2020-07-20: Where settlement looks possible, the District Commission can ask the parties for written consent, subject to prescribed exceptions. It refers the complaint to mediation only if the parties agree and give written consent.
